claim_verdicts.evidence: SDK 3.47.2 framework.dart:2201 BuildContext: 'A handle to the location of a widget in the widget tree.' ... 'BuildContext objects are passed to WidgetBuilder functions (such as StatelessWidget.build), and are available from the State.context member.' ... 'Each widget has its own BuildContext'. State.context: 'The location in the tree where this widget builds.'

navigator.dart:2927 Navigator.of: 'The state from the closest instance of this class that encloses the given context.' ... 'it walks the element tree' (findAncestorStateOfType). But material/app.dart: 'If [home], [routes], [onGenerateRoute], and [onUnknownRoute] are all null, and [builder] is not null, then no [Navigator] is created.' widgets/app.dart:530: 'The [Navigator] is only built if routes are provided (either via [home], [routes], ...)'. The unconditional 'MaterialApp creates a Navigator' needs the condition; DonHangApp passes home, so it holds here.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: Navigator.of(context) returns the closest Navigator above the given context. MaterialApp creates a Navigator when it is given a home (or routes); DonHangApp gives it home: ProductListScreen, so one exists.

claim_verdicts.evidence: navigator.dart Navigator.of doc: 'If there is no [Navigator] in the given `context`, this function will throw a [FlutterError] in debug mode, and an exception in release mode.' Assert text: 'Navigator operation requested with a context that does not include a Navigator.' theme.dart Theme.of doc confirms a build method's own context is 'above' the MaterialApp it returns: 'the `context` argument to the `build` function can't be used to find the [Theme] (since it's "above" the widget being returned)'.

material/theme.dart Theme.of: 'The data from the closest [Theme] instance that encloses the given build context.' BuildContext class doc: 'Theme.of(context) looks for the nearest enclosing [Theme] of the given build context.' Lesson says only 'the same kind of lookup', which this supports (Theme.of falls back to ThemeData.fallback rather than failing, but the lesson makes no claim about that).

git -C examples/don-hang show stage-1:DonHang.App/lib/screens/product_list_screen.dart lines 34-41: 'actions: [ IconButton( icon: const Icon(Icons.login), onPressed: () => Navigator.of(context).push( MaterialPageRoute(builder: (_) => LoginScreen(apiClient: widget.apiClient)), ), ), ],' — identical to the lesson block. context is the parameter of _ProductListScreenState.build (line 30).

git show stage-1:DonHang.App/lib/screens/login_screen.dart lines 29-33: 'await widget.apiClient.login(...); if (!mounted) return; Navigator.of(context).pushReplacement( MaterialPageRoute(builder: (_) => CreateOrderScreen(apiClient: widget.apiClient)), );' — identical to the lesson block; inside _LoginScreenState._submit, so context is State.context.

framework.dart State.mounted: 'Whether this [State] object is currently in a tree.' BuildContext.mounted: 'Accessing the properties of the [BuildContext] or calling any methods on it is only valid while mounted is true. If mounted is false, assertions will trigger. Once unmounted, a given [BuildContext] will never become mounted again.' State.context asserts: 'This widget has been unmounted, so the State no longer has a context (and should be considered defunct).'

product_list_screen.dart:11 at stage-1: 'const ProductListScreen({super.key, required this.apiClient});' — the constructor also accepts an optional key, so 'takes only an ApiClient' is literally too strong; 'requires only' is exact. main.dart:15-22: DonHangApp.build(BuildContext context) returns MaterialApp(... home: ProductListScreen(apiClient: apiClient)) — its context is above MaterialApp (confirmed by the Theme.of doc quoted in claim 3).
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: ProductListScreen's constructor requires only an ApiClient (key is optional); DonHangApp's build context is above the MaterialApp it returns.

claim_verdicts.evidence: Not opinion as used in the lesson ('without the navigator being passed down through each constructor'): the stage-1 source shows ProductListScreen has no navigator parameter (product_list_screen.dart:9-11) yet line 37 obtains one with Navigator.of(context), which per navigator.dart returns 'the closest instance of this class that encloses the given context'.

issues.text: Unlisted claim: a specific distance in the tree that nothing supports. In the lesson's own diagram, MaterialApp is one level above ProductListScreen and two above the IconButton; in the real element tree the Navigator sits many levels below MaterialApp (WidgetsApp, Navigator, Overlay, route widgets...) and many above the screen. 'Three' is neither.
issues.quote: How does one line in a screen find something created three levels above it
issues.fix: Replace 'created three levels above it' with 'created higher up in the tree'. No ledger entry needed after that.

issues.text: Claim 2 rephrased: MaterialApp creates a Navigator only when given home/routes/onGenerateRoute/onUnknownRoute (SDK material/app.dart: '...all null, and [builder] is not null, then no [Navigator] is created'). Stated unconditionally.
issues.quote: `MaterialApp` creates one, so any widget below `MaterialApp` finds it, however deep it sits
issues.fix: Write: "Here `MaterialApp` is given a `home`, so it creates one, and any widget below it finds it, however deep it sits," and update claim 2's text to the suggested_text in claim_verdicts.

issues.text: Claim 8 rephrased: the constructor is '{super.key, required this.apiClient}', so it also accepts a key. The lesson's 'asks only for' reads as 'requires', which is true, but the ledger text 'takes only an ApiClient' is not.
issues.quote: its constructor asks only for an `ApiClient`
issues.fix: Change the lesson to 'its constructor requires only an `ApiClient`' and set claim 8's text to the suggested_text in claim_verdicts.

issues.text: Section 4 says every `build` method receives a context. But the sign-in code uses `context` and `mounted` outside any `build` method, and I was never told where they come from. `mounted` is only explained in prose, not in Core concepts, and Connections says it comes from a `State` class that a later lesson teaches. I cannot tell why `context` exists in the sign-in code.
issues.quote: So after the `await`, the code first checks `mounted`, which is true only while the screen is still in the tree.
issues.fix: Add one sentence before this one: in a screen's class like `_LoginScreenState`, `context` and `mounted` can be used in any method, not only in `build`, and the next lesson shows where they come from.

issues.text: The lesson says `push` puts `LoginScreen` 'on top of the stack', which I read as 'above everything'. Then Try it (item 3) and quiz q3 (b) say `LoginScreen`'s context finds the navigator, so it must sit below the navigator in the tree. Nothing in the lesson says that. The diagram does not show `LoginScreen`, so I would get item 3 and q3 wrong or just guess.
issues.quote: and `push` puts a new `LoginScreen` on top of the stack.
issues.fix: Add one sentence after this: a screen pushed onto the navigator sits below the navigator in the widget tree (the 'top' of the stack is not above the navigator), so its context can find the navigator too.

issues.text: The dashed lookup arrow starts at `IconButton`, but section 5 says the context used belongs to `ProductListScreen`. I can't tell whose position the lookup starts from. Also, the section 4 prose never names the `IconButton` or `DonHangApp` nodes.
